skill.name: w-retro
skill.description: Run a focused retrospective after completed work by comparing the request with the outcome, identifying evidence gaps, and proposing up to three specific improvements.
skill.summary: Turn completed work into three practical improvements for the next task.
skill.author: blockmatic

security_audit.summary: The scanned skill is a 12-line, chat-only retrospective checklist with no executable code or detected security patterns. No prompt-injection, data-exfiltration, or business-logic abuse evidence was found in SKILL.md.

content.user_title: Review Completed Work and Improve Next Time
content.value_statement: Teams often finish tasks without recording what changed, what evidence was missing, or what should improve. This skill produces a concise, task-specific retrospective with up to three practical next steps.
actual_capabilities: Restates the requested outcome and compares it with what shipped.
Identifies skipped checks, unclear requirements, extra scope, and missing documentation.
Suggests up to three concrete changes for a similar future task.
Bases recommendations on the current task, plan, and checks.
Responds in chat without implementing changes, committing files, or opening pull requests.
limitations: It cannot inspect work that is not included in the conversation context.
It does not implement fixes, commit changes, or open pull requests.
Its recommendations depend on the quality of the task history and evidence provided.
It is not a replacement for formal incident reviews or compliance audits.

use_cases.title: Close a development task
use_cases.description: Review the request, shipped changes, checks, and documentation before closing a coding task.

use_cases.title: Improve team delivery
use_cases.description: Capture specific process gaps after a sprint item, project milestone, or cross-functional deliverable.

use_cases.title: Evaluate an AI-assisted workflow
use_cases.description: Compare the requested work with the AI-produced result and record better checks for the next session.
use_cases.target_user: AI tool users and technical leads

prompt_templates.title: Basic task retrospective
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the completed task in this conversation. State what was requested, what shipped, and one improvement for next time.
prompt_templates.scenario: For a quick review after a small task.

prompt_templates.title: Check process gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a retrospective on this completed task. Identify skipped checks, unclear requirements, extra scope, and missing documentation. Suggest no more than three specific changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: For a developer closing a work item.

prompt_templates.title: Compare plan and outcome
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the original request, plan, implementation, and validation evidence. Explain the most important differences and recommend up to three changes for the next similar task.
prompt_templates.scenario: For work with a written plan and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an AI-assisted delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a task-specific retrospective of this AI-assisted delivery. Separate outcome gaps from process gaps, cite the available evidence, and prioritize three changes that would improve the next session.
prompt_templates.scenario: For advanced workflow evaluation and team learning.

output_examples.input: We needed to add export filtering. The filter shipped and unit tests passed, but no browser test was run.
output_examples.output: Requested versus shipped: Export filtering was added and unit-tested. Evidence gap: Browser behavior was not checked. Next change: Add one browser test for filter selection and downloaded results.

output_examples.input: The task was to update the onboarding guide. The guide changed, but the examples were not checked against the current interface.
output: Requested versus shipped: The onboarding guide was updated, but example accuracy was not verified.
Process gap: The task lacked a user-interface consistency check.
Next changes: Review examples against the current interface and add a lightweight documentation checklist.

best_practices: Run the skill after checks are complete and the delivered result is known.
Provide the original request, completed work, validation evidence, and relevant constraints.
Prefer specific recommendations tied to this task over broad process advice.
anti_patterns: Do not use the retrospective as a substitute for implementing a required fix.
Do not request generic lessons without sharing task-specific evidence.
Do not turn a short retrospective into an unfocused list of every possible improvement.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after completing a task and recording the checks or evidence that support the result.

faq.question: What does the skill review?
faq.answer: It compares the request with the shipped result and checks for process or evidence gaps.

faq.question: How many improvements does it suggest?
faq.answer: It suggests at most three concrete changes for the next similar task.

faq.question: Can it change files or create commits?
faq.answer: No. It responds in chat and does not implement changes, commit files, or open pull requests.

faq.question: What context produces the best result?
faq.answer: Include the request, plan, completed work, validation checks, constraints, and known uncertainties.

faq.question: Does it replace a formal incident review?
faq.answer: No. It supports routine task learning and does not replace incident, compliance, or security review processes.
